Check a dataset for degenerate columns before building a DGF

preflight_dgf.Rd

Scans every column and reports the ones that tend to break, or quietly mislead, a profile: a column with a single value, an all-missing column, values too long for a date parser, a yes/no flag spelled several ways, zero-padded codes, duplicate columns, placeholder values, non-finite numbers, and timestamp columns with too many distinct values to store whole. It is much faster than create_dgf (about 40 seconds on a file of 568,000 rows and 199 columns, where the build took about 22 minutes with the formex release before its 2026-10-28 speed-up), and it reports every finding at once instead of the first failure.

Usage

preflight_dgf(df, max_chr = 1000L, smoke_n = NULL, seed = 1L)

Arguments

df

A data frame, or the path to a .csv file (read with every column as text, as create_dgf does).

max_chr

Values of at least this many bytes are reported as long_values. Defaults to 1000, the length at which base R's strptime() gives up.

smoke_n

NULL (the default), or a number of rows. If given, also runs create_dgf on a random sample of that many rows (written to a temporary folder, with the pre-flight off) and reports any failure as a smoke_test_failed finding that names the variable. A sample of a few thousand rows finds most crashes in about a minute, even on a file whose full build takes half an hour.

seed

Integer seed for the smoke-test sample. The session's random-number state is left as it was.

Value

A data frame with one row per finding and columns var_name, rule, severity ("error", "warn" or "info"), detail and suggestion; zero rows for a clean dataset. It has class dgf_preflight, with its own print() method.

Details

create_dgf runs this itself (see its preflight argument); call it directly to look at a dataset before committing to a build.

Missing means NA or blank (empty or whitespace-only), as in create_dgf. The rules, with their severity:

smoke_test_failed (error)

the sample build failed (only with smoke_n).

constant (warn)

every row has the same value.

single_value_with_blanks (warn)

one value plus blanks, e.g. an X/blank checkbox.

all_missing (warn)

no values at all.

duplicate_column (warn)

identical to an earlier column.

mixed_boolean_encoding (warn)

a flag written more than two ways (0, 1, true, false).

non_finite (warn)

Inf, -Inf or NaN.

placeholder_value (info, warn from 5% of rows)

0000000000, 9999, N/A, ... holding at least 0.1% of the rows.

long_values (info)

values of max_chr bytes or more.

leading_zero_code (info)

digit strings with leading zeros, which a number would lose.

high_cardinality_temporal (info)

too many distinct timestamps to store whole; see getOption("datagoodr.temporal.max_values").

create_dgf(preflight = "warn") reports errors and warnings; "error" stops on either.

See also

create_dgf

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  id    = sprintf("%03d", 1:40),
  year  = rep("2023", 40),                          # one value
  box_x = ifelse(seq_len(40) %% 4 == 0, "X", ""),   # one value plus blanks
  n     = rnorm(40)
)
preflight_dgf(df)
#> preflight_dgf: 4 columns, 40 rows: 0 error(s), 2 warning(s), 1 note(s)
#> 
#> [warn] constant: 1 column(s)
#>   year                               every row is '2023'
#>   -> no information to analyse; drop it, or record the value in the documentation
#> 
#> [warn] single_value_with_blanks: 1 column(s)
#>   box_x                              one value ('X') in 10 of 40 rows (25.0%); the rest are blank
#>   -> if a blank means 'no' this is a checkbox: recode to TRUE/FALSE; if a blank means 'not asked', leave blank; otherwise drop it
#> 
#> [info] leading_zero_code: 1 column(s)
#>   id                                 40 value(s) (100.0%) are digit strings with a leading zero, e.g. '001'
#>   -> keep as text: type it identifier or categorical, never number
